pending_diagnosis: DIAGNOSIS: Anti-NMDA Receptor Encephalitis secondary to an Ovarian Teratoma THE SMOKING GUN: Pelvic ultrasound/MRI revealing a mature cystic teratoma (dermoid cyst) of the ovary in a young female presenting with characteristic oro-facial dyskinesias, autonomic instability, and CSF pleocytosis. PATHOPHYSIOLOGY: Ectopic neural tissue contained within the ovarian teratoma triggers an autoimmune cross-reactivity, resulting in the production of IgG antibodies targeted directly against the GluN1 subunit of N-methyl-D-aspartate (NMDA) receptors in the central nervous system. Antibody binding causes cross-linking and irreversible internalization of these surface receptors, disrupting frontostriatal pathways and causing progressive psychosis, movement disorders, autonomic collapse, and central hypoventilation. Early tumor resection combined with aggressive immunotherapy is crucial for functional recovery.
